title: Clay, calcite and fire: the working vessels of Zlakusa
deck: In the Serbian village of Zlakusa, hand-wheel pottery brings local clay, ground calcite and open firing together in vessels made for preparing and storing food.

hero_media.creator: Milica Buha
hero_media.title: Potters from Zlakusa
hero_media.alt_text: Potters from Zlakusa shaping traditional vessels in a workshop

sources.title: Zlakusa pottery making, hand-wheel pottery making in the village of Zlakusa

sections.heading: A vessel designed for work
sections.text: Zlakusa pottery is unglazed hand-wheel ware associated with cooking and food storage. Its importance lies in an integrated process: locally understood raw materials, forming, surface treatment, drying and firing.

sections.heading: Clay tempered with calcite
sections.text: UNESCO’s documentation identifies a mixture of clay and ground calcite. Temper changes how a clay body handles and responds to heat; it is part of the vessel’s working design rather than a decorative addition.

sections.heading: Building on a hand wheel
sections.text: The maker shapes the vessel on a hand-operated wheel, controlling symmetry and wall thickness through repeated turning and pressure. The pace permits correction while requiring practiced coordination.

sections.heading: Seven to ten days of connected steps
sections.text: The formal record describes preparation, shaping, decorating, drying and firing across a multi-day sequence. Each stage constrains the next: uneven walls or rushed drying may emerge only when heat tests the vessel.

sections.heading: Knowledge held in practice
sections.text: Skills are transmitted in households and workshops, alongside public demonstration and local organisation. Inscription recognises that social system of knowledge; it does not freeze the craft or imply identical work.

sections.heading: Heritage is not a laboratory guarantee
sections.text: Documentation of thermal-food vessels does not establish universal performance, food-safety or durability for every pot sold under a regional name. Those questions depend on materials, firing, condition and use.
